faq: Do I need technical knowledge to use the plan?

No. The plan is written in everyday language, with each idea explained by what it does for a customer or your team. Technical notes sit at the end for a developer, so you can pass them on if you hire one.
Will you tell me if AI is not worth it for me?
Yes. If an idea costs more than it saves, or depends on data you do not have, we say so and mark it as skip. A short honest list is more useful than a long hopeful one.
What do you need from me?

A few minutes on the order form, plus view access to the tools you use, such as your store, helpdesk or spreadsheets. We never ask for passwords. You add us as a collaborator or share exports instead.
Can you build the features afterwards?
Yes, if you want. The plan ends with a suggested first feature, and the other services on this page cover building it. There is no obligation, and the plan is yours to hand to anyone.

desc:
AI feature planning for your business gives you a written, ranked list of where AI will save time or help customers, and where it adds risk for little gain. Ecom Swift LLC reviews how you work and returns a plan in plain words that your whole team can read.

## What is AI feature planning?

AI feature planning is a short piece of analysis done before any building starts. It looks at your processes, your customer journey and your tools, then decides which tasks suit AI and which do not. The output is a document: ranked ideas, rough running costs, the data each idea needs and a suggested first feature.

Think of it as a survey before construction. It costs far less than building the wrong thing, and it gives you something concrete to compare against vendor pitches.

## Why plan before you build

AI tools are easy to start and hard to judge. A chat widget can be live in an afternoon, yet nobody has asked whether customers want it, whether your content can support it or what it costs once traffic arrives. Teams often discover these answers after launch, when changing course is expensive.

Planning also protects you from the opposite mistake. Some businesses wait because the field feels confusing, and keep doing slow manual work that a simple tool could handle. A clear yes or no list removes the guessing from both directions.

## How a plan improves your decisions

A good plan changes where your money and time go. Instead of funding five experiments, you fund the one with the best balance of benefit, effort and risk. Instead of asking a developer for a vague AI feature, you hand over a build outline with the data, screens and limits already described.

The ranking depends on facts we can see, such as how often a task repeats, how clean your content is and how costly a wrong answer would be. We explain the reasoning behind each placement, so you can disagree with it and adjust.

## What a useful plan contains

- A clear description of each process reviewed, in your own terms.
- Ranked ideas, each with the problem it solves and who benefits.
- An effort and risk note beside every idea.
- A plain list of ideas to skip, with the reason.
- Rough monthly running costs for the strongest options.
- A checklist of data, documents and tools each idea relies on.
- A suggested first feature and why it comes first.
- A shortlist of providers and models that fit the first feature.
- Suggested wording for telling staff and customers what the feature does.
- Open questions that need an owner decision before work begins.

## What we do

You complete a short form about your business and give us read access to the tools you use, as a collaborator or staff user where the platform allows. We study the processes you choose, look at the content and data behind them and write the plan.

The Basic package covers one process with a ranked list and a short summary. The Standard package covers more processes, adds cost and data estimates and ends with a walkthrough call. The Premium package goes further, with effort and risk for each idea, a build outline for one feature, a provider shortlist, a wording plan and a written question and answer round. We state our assumptions openly so you can correct them.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Start with the tasks that repeat daily and follow clear rules.
- Share real examples, such as actual customer questions or support tickets.
- Ask who is accountable if the tool gets something wrong.
- Pick one first feature and measure it before adding more.
- Keep the plan as a living document you revisit.

**Avoid:**
- Adding AI because competitors have it, without a specific problem.
- Choosing a tool before knowing what data it needs.
- Using AI for decisions where one mistake is serious, with no human check.
- Ignoring running costs until the first invoice.
- Planning everything at once instead of one feature at a time.

## Who it is for

A shop owner hears about AI everywhere and wants an honest view of what would help a small team. An operations manager has several ideas from staff and needs them ranked. A founder is about to hire a developer and wants a clear brief first.

## What we need from you

We need a short description of your business, the processes you want reviewed, a few real examples of customer or staff questions and access to the relevant tools. Add us as a collaborator, staff or team user where the platform supports it, and never send passwords. If AI is not worth it for part of your business, we say so in the plan.
